newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan second-quarter GDP up 6.34 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan second-quarter GDP up 6.34 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's gross domestic product grew 6.34 percent year-on-year in the second quarter, down from the first-quarter's 6.83 percent but up sharply from a previous projection, an official of the government's statistics agency said on Friday.
The agency also revised its full-year 1997 projection to 6.58 percent from a May forecast of 6.24 percent.
The second-quarter's 6.34 percent rise sharply surpassed an average forecast of a 5.81 percent increase that resulted from August 13 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
The figure also outstripped the most recent forecast of the official statistics agency itself, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics.

The agency's most recent official forecast, issued on May 16, estimated second-quarter GDP at 5.61 percent, saying a devastating hog disease epidemic that erupted on March 20 would hurt economic growth in the second quarter.

An islandwide outbreak of hog foot-and-mouth disease has forced Taiwan temporarily to ban all fresh and frozen pork exports -- a US$1.55 billion a year industry -- and to slaughter nearly four million of the island's 14 million hogs.
Officials had estimated the hog disease would reduce Taiwan's GDP growth by between 0.39 and 0.50 percentage points.
Officials were upbeat about the better-than-expected economic growth.
"Domestic economy has walked out of a difficult situation and enters a bright future," a statement issued by the agency said.
It said the rosy outlooks were substantiated by robust economic growth and a low inflation.

It said the per capita gross national product for 1997 was expected to be US$13,467 and GDP growth 6.6 percent -- the highest annual growth since 1992's 6.8 percent, with the consumer price index seen at 1.7 percent -- the lowest growth since 1988.
Taiwan's economy has slowed significantly from its "Asian dragon" days of double-digit growth in the 1980s.

Growth in the mid-1990s was somewhere around six percent a year, but that rate dipped to 5.4 percent in the second half of 1995 during intense political and military tensions with long-time arch rival communist China.

Helped by a range of government stimulus plans and an easing of tensions with China, GDP growth rose back to above six percent in the second half of 1996, but settled at a disappointing 5.67 percent for all of 1996.
The fourth quarter of 1996 showed a promising 6.62 percent year-on-year rise, prompting officials to announce that a solid recovery was under way.
Agency director Wei Duan told a news conference that the second-quarter GDP rise was because of the smaller-than-expected impact of the hog epidemic and strong stock market performance.
The stock index rose 13 percent in the second quarter to close at the end of June at 9,030.28 points. It surged 30 percent in the first half.
